1	# WP-002: Trim Fields at Parse Time in `parseGitCredentials()`
     2	
     3	## Plan Context
     4	
     5	Address all remaining actionable deferred items from the `2026-06-26-multi-credential-support-rework-1` synthesis, including adding `'audit'` and `'info'` severities, extracting shared test helpers, resolving stale credential badges, adding a "Configure Credential" button, aligning field trimming, and unifying CSS variable naming.
     6	
     7	## Description
     8	
     9	Normalize all credential fields by trimming whitespace at parse time in `parseGitCredentials()`, eliminating the asymmetry where the API trims on write but the parser returns raw values.
    10	
    11	## Scope
    12	
    13	- `src/config/config.ts` — modify `parseGitCredentials()` to trim fields in both new-format and legacy-format branches
    14	- `src/tests/config.test.ts` — add tests for trim behaviour
    15	
    16	## Deliverables
    17	
    18	- In the new-format array branch: all four credential fields (`id`, `label`, `host`, `token`) are trimmed after length validation, before returning
    19	- In the legacy-format branch: `host` and `token` values are trimmed before constructing the `GitCredentialEntry`
    20	- Tests verifying trim behaviour for both format branches
    21	
    22	## Dependencies
    23	
    24	- None
    25	
    26	## Acceptance Criteria
    27	
    28	1. `parseGitCredentials()` returns trimmed values for all four credential fields (`id`, `label`, `host`, `token`) when processing new-format array entries with leading/trailing whitespace.
    29	2. `parseGitCredentials()` returns trimmed `host` and `token` values when processing legacy-format entries with leading/trailing whitespace.
    30	3. Existing valid `config.json` files with already-trimmed values parse identically (no backward compatibility break).
    31	4. New tests in `src/tests/config.test.ts` verify whitespace trimming for new-format entries across all four fields.
    32	5. New tests in `src/tests/config.test.ts` verify whitespace trimming for legacy-format entries.
    33	6. All existing tests continue to pass.
    34	
    35	## Active Pipeline Stages
    36	
    37	`implementation` → `qa` → `security-audit` → `code-review` → `documentation`
    38	
    39	## Estimated Complexity
    40	
    41	Low
    42	
    43	## Rationale
    44	
    45	Normalizing at the parser layer means all downstream consumers see trimmed values, eliminating the "consumers must trim before use" contract noted in `constraints.md`. The `config.json` file content is unchanged — trimming only affects the in-memory representation. The PUT route already trims on write, so round-tripping is idempotent.
    46	
    47	## Rejected Approaches
    48	
    49	- *Trim only at write time (current):* Leaves a documented contract that consumers must trim before use — easy to forget and produces subtle bugs.
    50	- *Trim at both endpoints:* Redundant — trim-at-parse is the single authoritative normalization point.
    51	
    52	## Notes
    53	
    54	No dependency on any other WP — can be worked in parallel. The trimming must occur after length validation to preserve the current validation semantics (validate raw values, then trim).
